class: Any money value (premium, P&L, value) that a consumer module re-computes from leg prices instead of reading it from the one calculation engine can silently drop a factor the engine applies (quantity, sign, instrument kind), so the consumer and the engine disagree.
mechanism: The rule engine summed signed per-unit LTPs itself to build its PREMIUM input and never multiplied by each leg's quantity, so strategies whose legs have different quantities (ratio spreads) got a wrong premium while equal-quantity strategies looked right.

first_seen.where: W-013 branch build/W-013-rule-engine @ d211f3b, backend/ofo/rules/inputs.py snapshot_from_strategy()
first_seen.evidence: BUY 75 x 23000 CE @ 100 / SELL 150 x 23200 CE @ 60: the rules' PREMIUM was -40 where the quantity-weighted net premium is +1,500 (red test run before the fix: 'assert Decimal('-40') == Decimal('1500)'; that case now lives in tests/rules/test_entry.py), and 'net credit at least 1,000' was NOT_TRIGGERED. Found by the independent verifier (AC-2/AC-4 fail); the golden Iron Condor has equal quantities, so every earlier test passed.

fix: engine.net_premium(strategy, PriceBasis) is the only net-premium formula (rupee total, credit positive, futures 0); the rules' NET_PREMIUM input reads it. Definition written in scenario-calculations.md section 3.

detection.note: The AST guard fails on any use of ltp/entry_price in backend/ofo/rules/ other than an 'is None' check; its self-test proves it flags the original re-implementation (a UnaryOp inside sum(), which a BinOp-only scan would miss). It covers only backend/ofo/rules/; other consumer packages (screens, monitoring) are not scanned yet. Sweep 2026-09-29 (case-insensitive ltp|last_price|entry|premium): backend/ofo/instruments/ does no money arithmetic; its only price hit is 'last_price' as a CSV column name in parser.py.
